audit.whatIsWrong: Five of seven rows disagreed with the packet chart. The page read Skill / Gangplank / Gangplank / Skill / Skill / Gangplank / Gangplank; the packet reads Karma / Karma / Skill / Gangplank / Gangplank / Gangplank / Gangplank.
audit.why: The prose backs the packet in every row: whys[0] 'soak it and farm', whys[1] 'concede the level', whys[2] 'a genuine coinflip', whys[3] 'you out-trade the poke war', whys[4] Cannon Barrage catches her escape, whys[5] 'you flip the lane', whys[6] 'own a squishy Karma all game'. The page had it giving Gangplank levels 2-3 — the exact two levels early says to soak and not trade in.
audit.corrected: Level 1 Skill 5/10 -> Karma 4/10; Level 2 Gangplank 5/10 -> Karma 4/10; Level 3 Gangplank -> Skill; Levels 4-5 and Level 6 Skill -> Gangplank. Both layers, one atomic group.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why says 'Reassess every all-in at 6 — Karma's ultimate changes the math too.' Karma has no level-6 spike: Riot's own R text says 'Mantra is available at level 1 and does not require a skill point.'
audit.why: It is the generic template line on a champion it cannot describe, and it tells the player to brace for a spike that already happened at level 1. What actually matters is that Mantra is 40/38/36/34 and Gathering Fire cuts that cooldown every time she lands a damaging ability — so she gets it back faster the more she pokes.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why now states Mantra is free from level 1 and costs no skill point. Inner Flame's 9s, Focused Resolve's flat 12s and its 675 range written into whys[1], spikes[2] and early.
sources: brief enemyKit R and P text

audit.whatIsWrong: Three errors. (1) 'Soulflare' is used twice as the name of Mantra-empowered Inner Flame; it is not a name in Riot's current text, which describes the Mantra Q bonus as a cataclysm after a short delay. Karma's R is simply Mantra. (2) spikes[2] calls Focused Resolve a 'self-root tether' — it roots the TARGET if the tether is not broken; Karma is not rooted. (3) The tether's break condition was stated only in the full layer, never in the content prose the player actually reads.
audit.why: Breaking the tether by leaving its 675 range or cutting line of sight is the entire counterplay to Karma's only lockdown, and the page's own dosFull entry knows it while the prose does not.
audit.corrected: Soulflare replaced with Mantra-empowered Inner Flame in whys[1] and wants.foe[1]; the self-root wording corrected in spikes[2]; the 675 break rule written into early.
sources: brief enemyKit Q, W and R text

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page mentions that Karma heals.
audit.why: Riot's W Mantra bonus: 'Karma strengthens the link, healing herself and extending the root duration.' In a long trade that heal is what undoes your chip, which is what the brief's needs-antiheal rule is pointing at.
audit.corrected: early now notes the Mantra'd tether heals her and ties that to anti-heal in long trades.

audit.why: The packet's suspect name 'Land Focused Resolve' is a false positive — correct name with a leading verb.

edits.before: Cannon Barrage wins fights you are not even in — watch the map. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Karma's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Cannon Barrage wins fights you are not even in — watch the map. Karma gains nothing at 6: Mantra is free from level 1 and costs no skill point.

edits.after: She free-pokes Inner Flame on 9s and roots you with Focused Resolve (W) into a Mantra cataclysm while you still have no answer — concede the level.

edits.after: Sheen/Essence Reaver plus a chained keg detonation bursts a squishy enchanter whose only defence is an Inspire shield and a 12s Focused Resolve root.

edits.after: Land Focused Resolve (W) to root you for a Mantra-empowered Inner Flame or a jungle gank

edits.before: Karma owns these first levels — her Q (Inner Flame) out-ranges Parrrley, and at level 1-3 your barrels have long cooldowns and so little HP she can pop them with a single auto to deny your poke, so don't try to trade. The CC to respect is her W (Focused Resolve) tether-root, not the Soulflare detonation people fear — hold your W (Remove Scurvy) to cleanse that tether and heal the chip rather than burning it on poke. Last-hit with the tip of Parrrley, eat the Q, and wait: she has no all-in to punish a passive lane, only poke.
edits.after: Karma owns these first levels — Inner Flame (Q) reaches 950 to your 625, and at 1-3 your kegs have long cooldowns and so little HP she pops them with one auto, so don't trade. The CC to respect is Focused Resolve (W): a 12s tether that roots you if you don't break it by walking out of its 675 range or behind terrain. Hold Remove Scurvy for that root, not for chip — and note a Mantra'd tether heals her, so anti-heal matters in long trades. Last-hit at the tip of Parrrley, eat the Q, and wait: she has no all-in to punish a passive lane.

notes: 'Soulflare' appears twice as the name of Karma's Mantra-empowered Q. It is not a name in Riot's current text — Data Dragon describes the Mantra Q bonus as a cataclysm and names the ultimate simply Mantra — so I replaced it rather than leave an unverifiable name on the page. Also fixed: Focused Resolve described as a 'self-root tether' (it roots you, not her), and the chart, which gave Gangplank levels 2-3 while the page's own 'early' paragraph says to soak the poke and not trade in exactly those levels. One thing I could not verify from the kit and therefore did not write: whether Remove Scurvy's cleanse actually removes the Focused Resolve root once it lands, or whether breaking the tether early is the only real out. The page asserts the cleanse in wants.you[1] and early; I kept the inherited claim but did not strengthen it.
